title: DEPUTYBENCH: Evaluating Contextual Safety in Enterprise Agents
attribution: Authors' own model results as stated on the arXiv abstract page; not reproduced or re-claimed here. Wording in the quotes below is the authors'.

claims.what: restricted execution rate, missing evidence vs explicit non-permission
claims.quote: restricted execution is more frequent with missing evidence than explicit non-permission: 10.3% versus 3.5% on 27 matched tasks, a 6.8-percentage-point difference (95% interval: 1.9-13.0; secondary analysis).

claims.four_privacy_tasks: requiring complete cumulative counts or person-specific consent
claims.quote: A post-hoc analysis locates 61 of 100 masked-condition executions in four privacy tasks requiring complete cumulative counts or person-specific consent.

claims.what: robustness of the gap and its size outside the four tasks
claims.outside_four_tasks: much smaller (no figure stated in the abstract)
claims.quote: The difference persists when the most error-prone model or the largest contributing task is excluded, but is much smaller outside those four tasks.
The concentration analysis describes task structure and audited outcomes, not an identified internal mechanism.
